executive_assessment.text: Historical dzud mapping and small-herd survey results differentiate Sukhbaatar and Khovd within a four-aimag study; national impact figures are dated to 2023-2024.

The assessment describes pasture degradation and movement to Otor grazing areas interacting with access/governance constraints and disputes. This does not establish armed violence or make mobile herders a threat category.
Warning, local response, household coping and protection-service gaps coexist with reported outreach and training. Targets and outputs are not evaluated resilience or GBV-reduction effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-05-27 reports: December 2023 risk mapping rated 90% of territory high or very high risk; surveyed herders with under 200 animals lost 61% in Sukhbaatar versus 6% in Khovd.

The dzud assessment describes pasture degradation, inter-aimag movement to Otor grazing areas, disputes with local users and a lack of systematic movement monitoring. Urban migration is a separate context; neither finding supplies armed-conflict counts.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 12 of 12 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No directly read source established climate-related effects on armed conflict or insecurity interrupting a named adaptation project; resource-competition conflict and GBV are recorded only as the reports describe them.
The UNFCCC National Adaptation Plan PDF timed out, and the UN Mongolia 2024 Common Country Analysis exceeded the reader limit; neither report's indexed text was used as evidence.
The World Bank's full social-protection study link returned an unexpected status; its claim is limited to the directly opened World Bank summary.
The FAO early-action policy-brief PDF redirected to an inaccessible reader; the brief was not used for claims.
The response and UNICEF situation reports describe the 2023-2024 dzud and are historical evidence, not statements of conditions or programme status in 2026.
The grazing pathway is a bounded source-stated resource-governance mechanism, not a national causal estimate or armed-conflict classification.
GBV is retained as a protection issue without deriving a complete causal pathway from co-occurrence or ethnic stereotypes.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
